title: lldp: Make dissector less greedy
description:
End of LLDPDU has been made an optional TLV as of 802.1AB-2016.  In these cases the LLDP dissector would consume the rest of the frame even if the bytes were not part of the LLDPDU.  Even when the End of LLDPDU was present, it would back up one byte (return -1) thus confusing other dissectors trying to find their data.

- Fixed the backup one byte issue.
- Added preference to toggle consuming unrecognized bytes as an "Unknown TLV" - defaults to not consume.
- Do not consider byte to be an unknown TLV if the TLV Type is unknown AND the TLV Len appears to run past the end of the reported TVB.

It could be, there may be some issues:
- need pip modules installed (pyspellchecker, not sure if collections, html.parser, urllib would be available)
- the output includes colouring escape codes(?), not sure how they'll appear in pipeline output (there is colouring, so maybe it'll be OK, maybe it does the equivalent of 'less -R')
- checking the wikipedia mispelled words is really slow (feels like around 30s), so would probably want to call with new flag --no-wikipedia
- some dissectors still output a lot (with a lot of false positives).  I can put it before the other checking scripts.  Its worth it (only) if some reviewers check the output...
Will resolve this thread and open an MR to check some of these issues.

"An" is fine in English IMO, it is an acronym where the L is pronounced as "ell".

https://blog.apastyle.org/apastyle/2012/04/using-a-or-an-with-acronyms-and-abbreviations.html

> a LAN schematic; an LAPD memo

LAPD the Los Angeles Police Department is "an"; LAPD the network protocol is "a" if you say it "lap d".

My apologies for the vagaries of English.
